name: Edge Hill University

settingEvidence.evidence: Our vibrant campus is in the heart of the North West of England, close to the market town of Ormskirk.

fees.text: £10,050 a year for UK students on full-time degrees starting in 2027/28. Edge Hill says this is the figure currently set, subject to Parliamentary approval and likely to rise with inflation. (The 2026/27 fee is £9,790.)

source.evidence: For the academic year 2027/28, the UK Full-Time tuition fee is currently set to £10,050.

livingCosts.text: University halls cost about £93–£175 a week in 2026/27, with utility bills included (Forest Court from £93; Founders East and West up to £175). Edge Hill says it guarantees a first-year room in halls for full-time UK undergraduates who apply on time.

source.evidence: £93 – £124 per week for 2026/27. Utility bills included.

openDays.text: Next open day: Saturday 21 November 2026, described as the last Open Day of the year. 2027 open day dates are not announced yet. A Virtual Open Day and student-led campus tours are also available.

source.evidence: Saturday 21 November 2026

contextual.summary: Edge Hill's Fair Entry Criteria can reduce your Level 3 entry requirements by up to two grades on most full-time courses if you meet any one of its listed criteria.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to a two-grade reduction in Level 3 entry requirements (most courses)

criteria.detail: Care experience: applicants who have been in care (listed together with estrangement).
Estrangement: applicants who are estranged from their families (listed together with care experience).
Those eligible for free school meals during their education.
Those who care, unpaid, for a family member or friend with an illness or disability, mental health condition or an addiction on a regular basis (excluding those with parental responsibilities).

POLAR Quintile 1: applicants entering university from a neighbourhood where there is low participation in higher education (the page does not name the POLAR version; it links to the OfS postcode checker).
IMD Quintile 1: students from low income households (check your postcode).
Students who have participated in one of Edge Hill's dedicated widening access programmes (completing the Edge Hill Access Programme gives access to the reduction).
Applicants who are the first in their family to attend university.

contextual.rulesText: You may qualify if you meet one or more of the criteria. Apply through UCAS as normal and indicate any criteria you meet; the admissions team assesses your application holistically and, if you are eligible, your Level 3 entry requirements are adjusted by up to two grades. All full-time courses are eligible except Medicine, Medicine with Foundation and Nurse Associate programmes, and you must be a home undergraduate student. For courses with GCSE requirements, interviews or extra checks you get extra support but must still meet all course-specific requirements.

source.evidence: You may qualify for the Fair Entry Criteria if you meet one or more of the following:

programmes.name: Edge Hill Access Programme
programmes.summary: A mostly virtual programme for Year 12 students from underrepresented backgrounds, with academic taster sessions, UCAS and student finance advice and social events; completing it unlocks Edge Hill's two-grade Fair Entry reduction.
programmes.whoCanApply: Students currently in Year 12 (sixth form) or Year 1 (college) who meet one or more of: care leaver, care experienced or estranged; eligible for free school meals; from a low-participation neighbourhood or low-income household; caring responsibilities; refugee status; or identify as Black, Asian or from another minority ethnic group.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Year 12 (sixth form) or Year 1 (college) and one or more of: care leaver, care experienced or estranged; eligible for free school meals; entering university from a neighbourhood with low participation in higher education or a low-income household (check your postcode); caring responsibilities; refugee status; identify as Black, Asian or from other minority ethnic groups.
benefits: Successful completion gives access to Edge Hill's Fair Entry two-grade reduction (not Medicine)
On-campus subject taster days for subject areas of your choice
Advice on researching courses, UCAS, personal statements, interview preparation and student finance
Progression to Edge Hill's on-course support programme, Thrive
programmes.offerReduction: 2-grade reduction through the Fair Entry Criteria (not Medicine), on successful completion
programmes.subjects: All subjects (taster days for subject areas of your choice)

runs.text: Not announced (the page says the programme will not be running for the 2025/26 academic year)

courses.notes: Edge Hill's economics degree: there is no standalone Economics BSc on its subject pages (the old course/economics-bsc page returns 'not found'). Accredited by the Chartered Management Institute (affiliate membership plus a CMI Level 5 Certificate in Management and Leadership). Course page shows a September 2027 start. If you have at least two A Levels, extra qualifications such as an EPQ, AS Levels not continued to A Level and General Studies all count towards the tariff points (no maximum number of qualifications).
